mainTopic: A טומטום found to be male and laws tied to birth; doubtful firstborns and the הרשאה between them
overview: This amud continues the discussion of a טומטום who is later found to be a זכר. אמימר says he does not reduce the בכור's extra share. רב שיזבי says he is not circumcised on the eighth day. רב שרביא says his mother is not טמאה לידה, because the פסוק requires a known זכר from birth. A משנה says a woman who miscarries a טומטום keeps the rules of both a male and a female birth. This conclusively refutes רב שרביא. The גמרא tries to save רב שיזבי by saying the משנה was ruling strictly out of doubt, but that answer ends with an unanswered difficulty. רבא then brings a ברייתא supporting רבי אמי: a טומטום and a doubtful בכור get no double share. This leads to רבא publicly taking back his ruling about two sons born in hiding, in favor of רבי ינאי's rule. Finally, the people of אקרא דאגמא ask שמואל what happens when a father names a different son as בכור than the one everyone presumed, and his answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A טומטום found male does not reduce the firstborn's extra portion
steps.stepSummary: אמימר adds that a טומטום later found to be a זכר is not counted when working out the בכור's extra share, because the פסוק requires a son at the time of birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: He also does not reduce the firstborn's portion, as it says, "And they bore him sons." He counts only if he is a son at the time of birth.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds a new ruling about a טומטום who turned out to be a זכר. He is not counted when working out how big the בכור's extra portion is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף shows this builds on the earlier rule that this person does not get a בכור's double portion himself. Now we learn he also does not shrink the בכור's extra share as a regular brother would. The source is "וילדה לו בנים": a brother counts only if he was a known son from the moment of birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, in addition to the earlier rule
Reduces, makes smaller
The firstborn's extra portion of the inheritance
At the time of birth

steps.confusionAlert: The topic is not a טומטום who stays unknown. It is one who was later found to be a זכר. The point is that he was not known as a זכר when he was born.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
He also does not reduce the firstborn's portion,
as it is said: "And they bore him sons"
until he is a son at the time of birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר אָמַר: אַף אֵינוֹ מְמַעֵט חֵלֶק בְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the earlier ruling, from before this section, that a טומטום found to be male does not take a double portion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום later found to be male is not counted in calculating the בכור's extra portion, since he was not a known son at birth.

steps.title: A טומטום found male is not circumcised on the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי adds that the eighth-day rule of מילה does not apply to a טומטום later found to be a זכר, because the פסוק links the eighth day to a baby born as a known זכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: He is also not circumcised on the eighth day, as the verse says, "If a woman conceives and bears a male... and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised." This applies only if he is a male from the time of birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי gives another ruling of the same kind. The eighth-day rule for מילה does not apply to this child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins "bears a male" with "on the eighth day he shall be circumcised." So the eighth-day rule depends on being a known זכר at birth. The מפרשים explain this means his מילה does not push aside שבת when the eighth day falls on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Is circumcised
On the eighth day
As the verse says
Conceives, literally 'bears seed'

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said:
He is also not circumcised on the eighth day,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה זָכָר״,
phrases.english: as the verse says: "If a woman conceives and bears a male"
"and on the eighth day he shall be circumcised"
until he is a male from the time of birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר: אַף אֵינוֹ נִימּוֹל לִשְׁמֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling. The same 'known at birth' idea is now applied to מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eighth-day מילה rule does not apply to a טומטום later found male, since he was not a known זכר at birth.

steps.title: His mother is not impure from the birth
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא adds that the mother of a טומטום later found to be a זכר does not become טמאה לידה, because the פסוק links her טומאה to bearing a known זכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: His mother is also not impure from the birth, as the verse says, "If a woman conceives and bears a male, she shall be impure seven days." This applies only if he is a male from the time of birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא adds a third ruling. The mother of this child does not get the טומאה of childbirth at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same פסוק as רב שיזבי, but reads its next words: "and she shall be impure seven days." Since her טומאה is tied to bearing a known זכר, he says a טומטום birth brings no טומאה. This ruling is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother
Ritually impure because of giving birth
Seven days, the impurity period after a boy is born

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
His mother is also not impure from the birth,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה זָכָר
phrases.english: as the verse says: "If a woman conceives and bears a male,
then she shall be impure seven days"
until he is a male from the time of birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָא אָמַר: אַף אֵין אִמּוֹ טְמֵאָה לֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel ruling. It uses the same פסוק as step 2 but applies it to the mother's טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who gives birth to a טומטום is not טמאה לידה, since the child was not a known זכר at birth.

steps.title: A משנה says the mother of a טומטום keeps both sets of rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שרביא from a משנה: a woman who miscarries a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס keeps the impurity rules of both a זכר and a נקבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A woman who miscarries a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס must sit out the impurity of both a male and a female. This is a refutation of רב שרביא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to contradict רב שרביא directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this mother is impure. Because we don't know whether the baby is male or female, she keeps the stricter side of both. רב שרביא said she has no birth טומאה at all, so the two clash head-on.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, using an earlier source
A woman who miscarries
A person whose gender is hidden, so we can't tell if male or female
A person with both male and female features
She 'sits', meaning she keeps the impurity period

phrases.english: They challenged:
A woman who miscarries a tumtum or a hermaphrodite
sits for a male and for a female.
phrases.notes: She keeps the rules of both a boy and a girl birth, since we don't know which one it was.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Sherevya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of רב שרביא in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שרביא's claim that a טומטום birth causes no טומאת לידה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly makes the mother of a טומטום impure under both the male and female rules, which contradicts 'no טומאה at all.'

steps.title: The refutation stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רב שרביא is conclusively refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and gives no answer for רב שרביא. His ruling is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A one-word 'תיובתא' means the objection is final. Only רב שרביא's ruling falls. The rulings of אמימר and רב שיזבי were not challenged here.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: רב שרביא's view is rejected: the mother of a טומטום does become impure, as the משנה says. The next steps ask whether the same משנה also refutes רב שיזבי's ruling on eighth-day מילה.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the challenge in step 4 as final.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב שרביא is refuted. The mother of a טומטום is impure, keeping the rules of both a male and a female birth.

steps.title: Is רב שיזבי refuted too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the same משנה that refuted רב שרביא also refutes רב שיזבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is also a refutation of רב שיזבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders whether the משנה that just knocked out רב שרביא also knocks out רב שיזבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's טומאה לידה and the eighth-day מילה come from the same פסוק about a woman who "bears a זכר." The משנה treats the birth of a טומטום as a real birth for טומאה. If so, that same פסוק should include him for eighth-day מילה as well, which goes against רב שיזבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggested conclusion that is often rejected.
A refutation, a decisive challenge from a תנאי source.
Circumcision, done on the eighth day even on שבת.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is a refutation of רב שיזבי?
phrases.notes: The link is that one פסוק (ויקרא 12:2-3) mentions both the mother's טומאה and the eighth day of מילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the refutation of רב שרביא (Step 5) to רב שיזבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שיזבי's ruling that eighth-day מילה does not apply to a טומטום later found to be a זכר (Step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats a טומטום birth as a birth under the פסוק for טומאה. The same פסוק governs eighth-day מילה, so it should apply to him too.

steps.title: The תנא was only in doubt and ruled strictly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not prove a טומטום counts as a זכר. The תנא was unsure and chose to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא was in doubt about it, so he ruled strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב שיזבי by reading the משנה as a ruling made out of doubt, not as a firm rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule for the mother is a חומרא based on uncertainty. It does not show that the פסוק definitely includes a טומטום. So for מילה the case also stays doubtful, and a doubtful case does not override שבת. This fits רב שיזבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage of the משנה or ברייתא being discussed.
He is in doubt about it.
Toward the strict side.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as saying a טומטום is surely a זכר for this law. According to this answer, it only says to be strict because we are unsure.

phrases.english: The תנא is uncertain about it,
phrases.notes: He's unsure whether the פסוק's "birth" includes a טומטום at all.

phrases.english: and he rules stringently.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source as a ruling made from doubt (ספק), not a firm rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that a טומטום birth fully counts under the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only a strict ruling out of doubt, so רב שיזבי's ruling on מילה can stand.

steps.title: If it's a doubt, the משנה should add נדה
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא were really unsure, the משנה should also have required the rules of נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said: she observes the rules for a זכר, for a נקבה, and of a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer. A real doubt would have needed one more strict rule that the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we are unsure whether a טומטום birth counts as a birth at all, then maybe there was no birth. In that case, blood she sees afterward would be ordinary נדה blood. A fully strict ruling would therefore add נדה, and the משנה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It opens a challenge based on the answer just given.
She shall observe (the rules of).
A woman who is טמאה from menstrual blood.
It should have said.

phrases.english: If so,
it should have said "she observes for a male, and for a female, and as a נדה"!
phrases.notes: If maybe there was no real birth, blood in the normally clean days after a birth would make her a נדה.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 7 that the תנא of the משנה was ruling out of doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full doubt includes the possibility that there was no birth at all. That would bring in the rules of נדה, yet the משנה leaves them out.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the challenge unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the question about נדה and moves on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain קשיא means the question is left open. It is weaker than a full תיובתא. So the answer in Step 7 is shaken, but רב שיזבי is not formally declared refuted the way רב שרביא was.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty. The question stands without an answer, but it is not a full refutation.

steps.whatToRemember: רב שרביא was refuted with a full תיובתא. The defense of רב שיזבי ends with only a קשיא, an open difficulty.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the exchange of Steps 6-8 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question from נדה remains unanswered.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אמי on the בכור's share
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא: "בן" excludes a טומטום, and "בכור" excludes a doubtful firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A ברייתא supports רבי אמי. "Son" means not a טומטום. "Firstborn" means not a doubtful case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the first ruling of the סוגיא and brings a ברייתא that backs it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this amud, רבי אמי ruled that a טומטום later found to be a זכר does not get the בכור's double share. Step 1 here is a different ruling, by אמימר: such a brother does not reduce the בכור's extra share. The ברייתא reads the word "בן" in the פסוק as excluding a טומטום, which supports רבי אמי. It adds from "בכור" that someone who is only possibly the firstborn does not get the double share either.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him.
Firstborn son, who receives a double share of the inheritance.
A doubtful case.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: the double share goes only to a definite son who is definitely the firstborn.
steps.whatToRemember: The בכור's double share needs a clear "בן" from birth and a definite "בכור". A טומטום or a doubtful firstborn does not receive it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rava said: It is taught in accordance with רבי אמי:
"Son" and not a טומטום,
"firstborn" and not a doubtful one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of מילה and טומאה and returns to רבי אמי's ruling, from before this amud, that a טומטום found to be male does not take the בכור's double share.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a טומטום later found to be a זכר does not receive the בכור's double share.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words "בן" and "בכור" in דברים 21.

steps.title: What does excluding a doubtful firstborn come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that "בן" excluding a טומטום fits רבי אמי, but asks what "בכור" excluding a doubtful firstborn is meant to rule out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that "a son" excludes a טומטום, as רבי אמי explained. But what case does "a firstborn, and not a doubtful one" come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the second half of רבא's ברייתא and asks what it is there for. This sets up the next step, which will name the case it rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first exclusion has a clear source in רבי אמי. The second one seems obvious, since nobody would expect a doubtful firstborn to get a double portion. So the גמרא wants to know who might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (it opens a contrast with a part that does not)
What does it come to exclude?
A doubtful case
A person whose gender cannot be seen

phrases.english: Granted, "a son" and not a tumtum —
that fits the teaching of Rabbi Ami.
But "a firstborn" and not a doubtful one —
what does that come to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the second clause of the ברייתא cited in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion or case the exclusion of a ספק בכור is aimed against.

steps.title: It rejects רבא's ruling about two sons born in hiding
steps.stepSummary: The exclusion rejects רבא's teaching that when two wives gave birth to sons in hiding, each son writes an authorization to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude what רבא taught: if two wives gave birth to two boys in hiding, each one writes an authorization to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is rejecting a ruling of רבא. רבא had said that two possible firstborns can team up and together collect the extra share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each son alone cannot prove he is the בכור, but between them one of them certainly is. With a הרשאה, each one stands in for the other, so together they can claim the extra share. The ברייתא's "not a doubtful one" says such a doubt gives no double portion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An authorization to act and collect for someone else (like a power of attorney)
In hiding, so no one saw which baby was born first
Taught publicly

phrases.english: To exclude what Rava taught,
for Rava taught:
two wives who gave birth
to two males in hiding,
phrases.notes: The two boys were born to two wives of the same man, and nobody knows which one came out first.

phrases.english: write an authorization to each other.
phrases.notes: Each gives the other the right to collect for him, so together they can claim the firstborn's extra share.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion rejects רבא's ruling that two possible firstborns born in hiding can collect the double portion through mutual authorizations.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges רבא with רבין's letter
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that רבין sent a ruling in the name of רבי ינאי: authorizations work only if the firstborn was once known and the sons were later mixed up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But רבין sent word: "I asked all my teachers and they told me nothing. But in the name of רבי ינאי they said: if they were known and later got mixed up, each writes an authorization to the other. If they were never known, they do not write authorizations."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's ruling using a tradition from ארץ ישראל. That tradition says that when the sons were born in hiding, the authorization does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי makes a distinction. If one son was once clearly recognized as the בכור and the boys were later mixed up, the authorizations work. If nobody ever knew who was first, which is exactly רבא's case of birth in hiding, no son was ever recognized as the בכור, and the authorizations do not help.

keyTerms.meaning: They were recognized: people knew which one was the firstborn
They got mixed up
However, but
But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But didn't Ravin send word:
"I asked all my teachers about this matter
and they did not tell me anything;

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: but this is what they said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
if they were recognized and in the end got mixed up,
they write an authorization to each other.
If they were not recognized,
they do not write an authorization to each other!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא, וְהָא שְׁלַח רָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that sons born in hiding write authorizations to each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי allows authorizations only when the firstborn was once identified. Birth in hiding means he never was, so רבא's ruling contradicts רבי ינאי.

steps.title: רבא publicly admits his mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets up a speaker and announces that his earlier teaching was a mistake, and that the הלכה follows רבי ינאי's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then set up an אמורא to speak for him and taught: "What I told you was a mistake on my part. This is what they said in the name of רבי ינאי: if they were known and later mixed up, they write authorizations to each other. If they were never known, they do not."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts רב פפא's challenge. He publicly takes back his ruling and teaches רבי ינאי's rule in its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The final הלכה: two sons born in hiding, when nobody ever knew who was first, cannot use authorizations to collect the double portion. This is the case the ברייתא's "בכור, and not a doubtful one" excludes. Only when a known firstborn later got mixed up can the brothers team up.

keyTerms.meaning: Then, afterward (he went back)
He set up a speaker to repeat his lecture aloud to the crowd
They are a mistake on my part

steps.whatToRemember: A firstborn who was never known gets no double portion, even through authorizations. If a known firstborn later got mixed up with his brother, they can write authorizations to each other and collect it together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much weight the תורה's word "בכור" carries: the double portion goes only to someone who was at some point clearly the firstborn. It also shows a great אמורא publicly admitting a mistake.

phrases.english: Rava then set up an amora for it,
phrases.notes: The אמורא was the speaker who repeated the lecture loudly to the crowd, so everyone would hear the correction.

phrases.english: and taught:
"The things I told you
are a mistake on my part.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: But this is what they said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
if they were recognized and in the end got mixed up,
they write an authorization to each other;
if they were not recognized,
they do not write an authorization to each other."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא accepts the challenge of Step 13 and retracts the ruling quoted in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי ינאי: authorizations work only if the firstborn was once identified and later mixed up. Sons born in hiding, never identified, cannot claim the double portion.

steps.title: בני אקרא דאגמא ask שמואל about a father contradicting a presumption
steps.stepSummary: The people of אקרא דאגמא ask שמואל: if one son was presumed to be the בכור, and the father says another son is the בכור, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: בני אקרא דאגמא sent a question to שמואל: 'Teach us, our master. Everyone presumed that this son was the בכור. Then his father said about a different son, "He is the בכור." What is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. A community sends שמואל a real question about a clash between a חזקה and what the father says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two pieces of evidence pull in opposite directions. Everyone already believed son A was the בכור. Now the father, who usually is believed about which son is his בכור, points to son B. The question is which one wins.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of Akra De'Agma, a town in Bavel
'Teach us, our master', a polite way of opening a question to a rabbi
Presumed; everyone treated it as known
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Here the father is not naming a בכור when nobody knew who it was. He is going against what everyone already believed, and that is why there is a real question.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי אַקְרָא דְאַגְמָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: The people of Akra De'Agma sent to Shmuel:
Teach us, our master:
If they presumed about this one that he is the firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר אָבִיו עַל אַחֵר ״בְּכוֹר הוּא״, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and his father says about another son, 'He is the firstborn,' what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי אַקְרָא דְאַגְמָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל, יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that comes after the discussion of doubtful firstborns and הרשאה in steps 12–14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the father's word goes against an existing חזקה about which son is the בכור, which one decides who gets the firstborn's share?

steps.title: שמואל answers that the sons write an authorization
steps.stepSummary: שמואל replies that they write a הרשאה, which treats the case as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל sent back to them: 'They write a הרשאה.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל begins his answer: the sons write a הרשאה, so neither the חזקה nor the father's word fully wins. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הרשאה is used when we don't know which son is really the בכור. So by telling them to write one, שמואל is saying the case stays doubtful. The father's statement is not enough to cancel the חזקה, and the חזקה is not enough to ignore the father.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent back to them
They write
A written power of attorney that lets one person act for another

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties into steps 13–14. There the גמרא said a הרשאה works only in certain doubt cases, so שמואל's answer will need to be understood in that light.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
They write an authorization
phrases.notes: He means the two sons each write one, so that between them they can claim the firstborn's extra share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sons write a הרשאה. The case is handled as a doubt, not given fully to either son.
